**SECTION D: ESSAY.** Write an essay of 250-300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** You have witnessed some instances of corruption in your school. Write a letter of complaint to the principal of your school citing the instances and suggest what can be done to stop this practice. Your school is Government High School Ako and the post office box is 157. Your name is Paul Nang.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC sanctionne autant le respect du format imposé (lettre administrative de plainte, discours devant un conseil municipal, essai structuré en causes/problèmes/solutions) que le contenu. Une lettre de plainte respecte les codes administratifs (adresses, objet, formule d'appel et de politesse) tout en restant factuelle sur les faits dénoncés ; un discours devant des élus doit présenter à la fois les avantages et les inconvénients d'un projet pour paraître crédible, jamais un plaidoyer à sens unique ; un essai « causes, problems and solutions » suit strictement cette progression en trois temps. Comme le sujet propose un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun l'un des formats possibles.

## Topic 1 - Formal letter of complaint (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Government High School Ako
P.O. Box 157

The Principal
Government High School Ako

Subject: Complaint regarding instances of corruption within the school

Dear Sir,

I am writing to bring to your attention several instances of corruption that I have personally witnessed within our school, which I believe require your urgent intervention.

On more than one occasion, I have seen certain students paying money directly to a teacher in exchange for marks they had clearly not earned through their own work. I have also heard from several classmates that some students avoid punishment for serious misconduct simply by paying a "fine" to a staff member, an arrangement that never appears in any official school record.

These practices are deeply unfair to the majority of us who work honestly for our results and respect the school's rules without expecting special treatment. If left unaddressed, they risk teaching an entire generation of students that success and consequences can both be bought, a lesson no school should ever allow to take root.

I would respectfully suggest that the school administration introduce an anonymous reporting system so that students who witness such practices can report them without fear of being identified or victimised. I would also suggest that all exam scripts and disciplinary decisions be systematically countersigned by a second staff member, making it harder for any single individual to manipulate the outcome alone.

I trust that you will take this matter seriously, and I remain available to provide further details in person if that would be helpful.

Yours faithfully,

Paul Nang

**SECTION D: ESSAY.** Write an essay of 250-300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** The town you come from, Mindili, has many undeveloped and unexploited tourist attractions. Write a talk you will deliver to members of the town council convincing them to develop these attractions because of the advantages of tourism to your town. Also tell them of the disadvantages it might cause.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Speech to the town council (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Honourable members of the council,

Thank you for allowing me to speak today about something I believe could transform our town, Mindili: the tourist attractions we have long overlooked.

Mindili is home to natural sites, waterfalls, caves and forest trails, that many visitors would travel a long way to see, yet they remain almost entirely undeveloped. Investing in these attractions could bring real advantages to our community. Tourism would create new jobs for our young people, as guides, in hospitality, and in the sale of local crafts and produce. It would also justify improvements to our roads and electricity supply, improvements that would benefit every resident of Mindili, not only visitors. Finally, a modest but steady flow of tourists could support local businesses that currently struggle for customers throughout the year.

I would be dishonest, however, if I did not also mention the disadvantages such development might cause. An influx of outsiders can sometimes bring rising prices that make daily life harder for long-time residents. It can also place unexpected pressure on our natural sites themselves, since poorly managed tourism sometimes damages the very attractions it is meant to showcase. There is also a risk, without careful planning, of some of our traditions becoming a mere spectacle for visitors rather than a living part of our community.

I am not asking you to ignore these risks. I am asking that we develop these attractions thoughtfully, with clear rules protecting both our environment and our traditions, so that Mindili can benefit from tourism without losing what makes it worth visiting in the first place.

Thank you.

**SECTION D: ESSAY.** Write an essay of 250-300 words on any one of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** Unemployment: Causes, Problems and Solutions.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Essay: causes, problems and solutions (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Unemployment remains one of the most pressing challenges facing young people in our country today, and understanding its causes is the first step towards addressing it seriously.

Several factors explain the scale of the problem. Our education system still produces many graduates trained for a narrow range of office jobs, while the economy increasingly needs practical, technical skills that schools rarely teach in sufficient depth. Population growth has also outpaced the creation of new jobs, meaning that even a growing economy struggles to absorb every young person entering the labour market each year. Finally, limited access to credit makes it very difficult for young people with genuine business ideas to start their own enterprises rather than waiting for a formal job that may never come.

The problems caused by unemployment go far beyond the individual. Families lose an important source of income, sometimes pushing them further into poverty. Prolonged unemployment can also push some young people towards crime or hazardous informal work as a last resort, undermining both their own safety and the wider stability of their community. At a national level, this waste of youthful energy and talent represents a real economic loss for the country as a whole.

Solutions exist, though none of them is simple. Technical and vocational training should be expanded and better funded, so that education matches the real needs of the job market. Access to microcredit for young entrepreneurs should be made easier and less bureaucratic. And government incentives for companies that hire and train young workers could encourage the private sector to become part of the solution rather than remaining on the sidelines.

Unemployment will not disappear overnight, but a clear understanding of its causes gives us a real chance to reduce it step by step.
